title: Invited teammates could never sign in
problem: An invite stored a token but never returned a link or sent an email, there was no accept page, and registering always created a new workspace. An admin had no way to add a teammate who could then log in.
fix: The invite returns a link the Team page shows with a copy button. The accept page lets the invitee set a name and password and joins them to the inviting workspace with the invited role. Tokens are single use and expire.

title: Builder Knowledge tab empty when the API is on another origin
problem: The tab fetched a relative /api URL, which 404s whenever the web app and the API are served from different ports, so it always said there were no collections.
fix: It goes through the shared API client like every other call.

title: No way to pin an agent to an Atlas graph from the UI
problem: Pinning needed model_config.atlas_graphs, which had no control anywhere.
fix: The Knowledge tab lists Atlas graphs with a checkbox each and offers to add the Atlas tools when none are on the canvas.

title: Pipelines could only be built by drag and drop
problem: Steps could only be dragged onto the canvas, edges only drawn by dragging handles, Dependencies was read only and the template buttons did nothing.
fix: Clicking a palette step adds it, Dependencies is a checkbox list that creates and removes edges, the templates insert their steps, and agent steps have an agent picker.

title: Publishing called the endpoint twice and overwrote a marketplace submission
problem: After the dialog succeeded a second publish with no body reset visibility to the organisation and marked the agent active, undoing a pending marketplace review.
fix: The second call is gone.

title: Publishing a pipeline failed with 400
problem: The publish check required a system prompt, which pipelines do not have.
fix: The check is skipped for pipelines.

title: Saving a pipeline dropped its error handling settings
problem: timeout, on_error, error branch, switch and merge settings were lost on Save Draft.
fix: They save and reload.

title: Chat dropped stream events split across network chunks
problem: When an event line and its data line arrived in different chunks the event was lost.
fix: The parser keeps the pending event name across chunks.

title: Code Runner never updated an asset while it was being analysed
problem: The list did not refresh, so an upload showed analyzing until the page was reloaded, and an asset opened during analysis kept Run disabled after it finished.
fix: The list polls while anything is pending and the open asset follows it.

title: Code asset zipped as one folder failed to run
problem: The analyzer looked inside the single top-level folder that most zips have, but execution ran from the archive root, so the entrypoint was not found and the test run failed with exit code 2.
fix: The analyzer and the runtime share one rule and both run from inside a lone top-level folder, including assets uploaded before the fix.

title: Knowledge base page had no way into search
problem: After uploading, the detail view offered no search, and an empty search showed nothing at all.
fix: The detail view has search and Use in an agent buttons, and an empty search says why it found nothing.

title: Re-run from the Flight Recorder opened an empty chat
problem: The prefill was read and never used, and chat had no link back to the run it produced.
fix: Re-run fills the composer and every answer links to its run.

title: Schedule triggers could not be run on demand
problem: Only webhook triggers had a test action.
fix: Every trigger has Run now, which dispatches it like the scheduler and links to the run.

title: Icon-only buttons without labels and no duplicate for your own agents
problem: The share submit and key revoke buttons had no text or label, and Duplicate only existed for built-in agents.
fix: Both buttons are labelled and Duplicate works for any agent you can access.

title: Marketplace option offered to roles that cannot publish
problem: Users without the publish feature saw the option and got a 403.
fix: The option is disabled with the reason and how to get access.

title: New users had no guidance on where to start
problem: A new teammate landed on an empty dashboard with no path through the product.
fix: A Getting started checklist ticks off from the user's own work and links to the next step. Every resource page offers Use in an agent.

title: Builder tool nodes stretched across the canvas
problem: Tool nodes had no maximum width, so once every tool carried a full description the node grew to the length of the sentence, covered the canvas and pushed the agent node out of view.
fix: Canvas nodes have a fixed width, the description is truncated and shown in full on hover.

title: Sub-agents ran under the platform key instead of the caller
problem: invoke_agent searched and executed sub-agents with a shared platform key, so delegated runs were attributed to the key's owner and a user could invoke agents they had no access to.
fix: Sub-agents run as the user who started the parent run with a short-lived token, follow the normal access rules, are linked to the parent run and stop at a depth of three. An agent cannot call itself.

title: Any member could edit or delete another member's Atlas graph
problem: Atlas only checked the tenant, so every member could list, change, export and delete every graph in the workspace.
fix: Atlas follows the owner, admin or share rule the other resources use, with view and edit shares and a read-only notice.

title: Lists did not say which items were yours
problem: Code assets, knowledge bases and Atlas graphs from the platform and from teammates appeared alongside your own with no owner shown, and the getting started checklist counted them as your work.
fix: Each item carries a Yours, Shared by or Platform badge, controls you cannot use are hidden, and the checklist counts only your own work.

title: Atlas grounded search never matched instance nodes
problem: atlas_search_grounded only looked at concept nodes, so asking about a named supplier such as Nordtek returned found false and the agent gave up. It also returned nothing useful when a concept had no bound documents.
fix: It matches any non-document node with exact matches first, returns the node's relationships, and when nothing matches lists the labels in the graph so the agent can retry.

title: Knowledge bases picked in the builder were never attached to the agent
problem: The builder listed knowledge bases with a limit the API rejects, the error was swallowed, and no grant was written. An agent built from Use in an agent on a knowledge base or Atlas graph could not search the documents it was built for.
fix: The agent save carries the selected knowledge bases and the API writes or removes the grants, telling the builder about any it was not allowed to attach.

title: Builder save failures were silent
problem: A failed create or update was ignored, so the builder looked saved while nothing was stored.
fix: Failures show a banner with the server's reason and keep the changes in place.

title: Any member could edit, run or download another member's code asset
problem: Update, test run and download only checked the workspace, not the owner or shares.
fix: View needs ownership, a share or a platform asset. Edit needs ownership, an edit share or admin.

title: Atlas could bind a knowledge base the caller cannot read
problem: Binding, syncing and instance import only checked the workspace, so a graph could pull in documents from a private knowledge base.
fix: Atlas uses the knowledge base read check.

title: Any member could share another member's knowledge base
problem: The share check let anyone in the workspace share any knowledge base, based on an old note that collections had no owner.
fix: Only the owner or an admin can share it.

title: Share, delete and upload offered to people who cannot use them
problem: Code Runner and Knowledge detail panes always showed Share and Delete, and the upload area showed for read-only viewers, each ending in a 403. Atlas graphs were missing from the share dialog types.
fix: The controls follow can_manage and can_edit from the API, read-only viewers see who to ask, and the share dialog knows Atlas graphs.

title: Publish dialog left the page when sharing failed
problem: When some specific-people shares failed the dialog navigated to chat at once, so the error was never seen.
fix: The dialog stays open with the failures and offers Continue to the agent.

title: Sub-agents called outside chat ran under the platform key
problem: Several runtime paths built the tool registry without the calling user, so invoke_agent fell back to the platform key for pipelines, agent steps, queued runs with MCP tools and A2A calls.
fix: Every path passes the calling user through, so sub-agents always run as that user.

title: Invite links were not rate limited
problem: Looking up an invite and accepting it were outside the login rate limit, so invite tokens could be guessed at full speed.
fix: Both go through the same per-address limit as login and register.

title: Pipeline agent picker hid your agents and sat on the wrong tab
problem: The Agent Step picker loaded only the first 100 agents by name, so in a workspace with more agents your own could be missing, and it was on the Arguments tab while the General tab a user opens first had no way to pick an agent.
fix: The picker pages through every agent, lists yours first, and sits on the General tab with the task. The inline prompt and model stay under Arguments.

title: Getting started and the agent step config asked for more agents than the API returns
problem: Both requested 200 agents from an endpoint capped at 100, the request failed validation, and the checklist never ticked Build an agent while the agent step config listed nothing.
fix: The checklist asks within the cap and the config pages through every agent.

title: Pipeline steps referenced by their label got nothing
problem: The builder gives steps generated ids, so a step labelled score is really step_1790931980212_b8m3. Writing {{score.response}} resolved to nothing, the next step ran on an empty input and the final LLM call invented an answer while the run reported success.
fix: A unique step label works anywhere an id does, in the engine and the validator. An id still wins over a label of the same name and an unknown name is still a validation error.

title: Flight Recorder named pipeline steps by tool
problem: Every pipeline step showed its tool name, so two agent steps both read agent_step and could not be told apart.
fix: Steps carry their label through the result and the recorder shows it, with the id on hover.

title: SDK playground could not send a message to a plain agent
problem: For an agent with no declared input variables the live inputs panel had no message box and told the user to leave the message blank, so every live run sent the word run and the agent had nothing to work on.
fix: The panel shows a message box for such agents and the live run sends what was typed.

title: Pipeline runs in chat never showed the answer
problem: A pipeline routed through the worker queue publishes its result only on the done event. The chat relay passed that event through without text, so the chat showed the step list and no answer, and each step was named by its generated id.
fix: The relay sends the final answer as text when the run streamed none, and node events carry the step label the chat shows.

title: Agents run as pipeline steps lost their tool settings
problem: An agent step loaded the agent's prompt, model and tools but not its tool configuration, so an agent bound to a code asset or an Atlas graph could not find it inside a pipeline. The scorer replied that its code asset was unavailable and every later step built on that.
fix: An agent step applies the agent's tool configuration, asset schemas and pinned graphs exactly as a direct run does.

title: SDK playground dropped a message typed while the agent was loading
problem: Selecting an agent loads its input schema in the background and then reset every input, so a message typed in the meantime was silently replaced by an empty one.
fix: Values typed while the schema loads are kept.

title: API keys were revoked on a single click
problem: The revoke button removed the key immediately with no confirmation, so a stray click broke every client using it.
fix: Revoking asks for confirmation and names the key.

title: Dialogs did not close on Escape
problem: The share, export, version history, AI builder, AI validate and resource share dialogs ignored Escape and had no dialog role, so a keyboard user was stuck behind the overlay.
fix: All six close on Escape and are marked as modal dialogs.

title: No way to upload a new version of a code asset
problem: Fixing a bug in uploaded code meant creating a new asset and rewiring every agent and pipeline that used the old one.
fix: Upload new version replaces the code behind the same asset. It goes live only if it analyses cleanly, earlier versions are kept up to a limit and can be restored, uploads are serialised per asset and every change is audited.

title: A failed code asset did not say why
problem: When analysis failed the asset showed a generic message and the raw notes, with no statement of what to change or how to fix it in place.
fix: A failed asset shows the analyzer's reason and points to Upload new version.

title: Sandbox fetch of large code assets had no valid credentials
problem: Assets too large to inline were fetched by the sandbox with a token that only the test endpoint ever set, so agent runs of large assets failed, and the token was the caller's own which a shared agent's user may not have.
fix: The runtime signs a ten minute token scoped to that one asset and the sandbox fetches through a route that accepts only that token.

title: Bulk delete removed any agent in the workspace
problem: The bulk delete endpoint hard deleted every listed agent in the tenant with no ownership check, so any member could permanently remove a teammate's or a built-in agent, bypassing the archive the single delete uses.
fix: Bulk delete follows the single delete rules: owner or admin only, built-in agents refused, agents are archived, and agents something depends on are skipped unless confirmed.

title: Deleting something others used gave no warning
problem: Deleting an agent, a code asset or a knowledge base gave a plain confirm with no mention of the pipelines, agents, triggers or Atlas graphs that used it. Those broke silently afterwards and the triggers kept firing.
fix: Each delete first lists what uses the item with links, refuses unless confirmed, and on a confirmed delete switches off the agent's triggers and unbinds graphs and grants. Deletes are audited.

title: Pipelines kept running deleted agents
problem: A pipeline step looked its agent up by slug regardless of status, so an archived agent still ran inside pipelines, and a direct call to it said only that it was not in an executable state.
fix: A step whose agent was deleted fails with a message naming the step and the deleted agent, and a direct call says the agent was deleted.

title: Delete buttons misled about what happened
problem: The knowledge base detail delete reported success even when the server refused, and every agent card offered Delete to people who could not delete it while saying it could not be undone, though agents are archived and can be restored.
fix: Delete reports the server's answer, agent delete only appears for the owner or an admin, and the dialog says what is kept.

title: Deleted agents could not be restored
problem: Deleting an agent archived it, but nothing in the product listed archived agents or brought one back, so a mistaken delete needed database access to undo.
fix: Manage Agents has a Recently deleted list. Restore brings back the agent's previous status and switches its triggers back on, and both directions are audited.

title: Version revert and switched-off triggers gave no feedback
problem: Reverting an agent to an earlier version reloaded the page whether or not the revert worked, and a trigger switched off because its agent was deleted looked the same as one paused by hand.
fix: Revert reports success or the server's reason, and such a trigger reads Off, agent deleted, with a hint that restoring the agent switches it back on.

title: Agent page offered edit, share and versions to people who could only run it
problem: Edit, Share and Versions showed on every agent page, so a teammate an agent was shared with to run hit a 403 from each.
fix: The agent detail says what the caller may do, Edit and Versions show to editors and Share to the owner or an admin.

title: Flight Recorder kept only the first 500 characters of a tool result
problem: Tool results were stored as a 500 character preview, so the end of a result, often the part that explains a failure, could not be seen after the run.
fix: Each tool call and pipeline step keeps its full result up to a configurable cap of 8000 characters, marked when cut, and the recorder shows it.

title: Owners could not save edits to an existing agent
problem: The builder sends the agent type with every save and the API refused any agent type from a non-admin, even unchanged, so a member editing their own published agent got a 403 and the change was lost.
fix: Only an actual change of agent type needs an admin. The builder shows the server's reason when a save is refused.

title: Builder did not show knowledge bases granted elsewhere
problem: The builder read an agent's knowledge bases from its saved config, so collections granted from the Knowledge page showed unticked, and saving could appear to drop them.
fix: The agent detail returns the agent's actual grants and the builder edits that list.

title: Builder let people edit agents they could not save
problem: Someone an agent was shared with to run could open it in the builder and change everything, and only found out on save that nothing would be kept.
fix: The builder says up front that the agent is read only for them and links to Duplicate.

title: Reloading the API after a new migration left it unable to start
problem: deploy.sh reload pointed the API container at the new image but left the db-migrate init container on the old one, which does not know the newest migration, so the new pod crash looped. Reload also never applied migrations.
fix: Reload moves every container built from the service image, init containers included, and runs migrations after an API reload.

title: My Agents always counted zero
problem: The agent list left out creator and tenant ids, so My Agents showed 0 and the header said 0 agents available while the user's agents were on screen, and sub-agent lookup without a user found nothing.
fix: List rows carry creator, tenant, published state and timestamps.

title: Restoring an earlier agent version always failed
problem: The revert endpoint read a field agents do not have and compared the role to plain strings, so every revert errored, and it applied the state before the chosen version rather than the version itself.
fix: Restore puts the chosen version back, records the replaced state as a new revision, keeps knowledge base grants in step and is audited.

title: Grouped agent view had no delete
problem: The default grouped layout used a card without the delete control, so agents could only be deleted after switching to the grid.
fix: Both layouts offer delete to the owner or an admin.

title: Any member could see, change or fire every trigger in the workspace
problem: The trigger list returned every trigger in the tenant with its webhook URL, which contains the secret that fires the agent, and any member could edit, pause or delete any trigger or add one to an agent they could not run.
fix: Members see and manage triggers they created or that belong to their own agents, admins see all, and creating a trigger needs run access to the agent.

title: Agent trigger link always opened a create form over all triggers
problem: Following Schedule from an agent opened the create dialog even when the agent already had triggers, behind it the list showed every trigger, and the agent picker held only the first twenty agents.
fix: The link shows that agent's triggers with a Show all chip, opens the create form only when there are none, and the picker lists every agent.

title: A failed pipeline step showed no reason in chat
problem: When a pipeline step failed, chat showed the step as failed with no message, and the error banner was not announced to screen readers.
fix: The failed step shows its error under it and the chat error banner is an alert.

title: The original version of an agent could not be restored
problem: Version history could restore a saved version but not the state before the first saved change.
fix: History ends with an Original entry that restores the state before any saved change.

title: Restoring a version reloaded the page and hid the result
problem: After a version restore the agent page did a full reload, so the confirmation disappeared before it could be read.
fix: The page refreshes the agent in place and the confirmation stays.

title: Failed runs showed the raw provider error in chat
problem: When the model provider refused or could not be reached, chat showed the provider's raw response, for example Error code 401 with a JSON body, which told the user nothing about what to do.
fix: Known failures read in plain language with who can fix them, and the raw text sits under Details.

title: An agent that ran out of steps returned nothing usable
problem: When an agent hit its iteration limit its whole output was the text Max iterations reached, so a pipeline step built on it, such as PharmaVigil's MedDRA coding, passed nothing downstream and the case came out with no coded terms.
fix: At the limit the agent gets one more turn to answer from what it already gathered, in the format it was asked for, and says what it could not establish.

title: Seeded ML models were invisible to the agent runtime on local installs
problem: Locally the runtime mounted the shared model volume over /data/ml-models while the API, which writes seeded and uploaded models, did not, so the runtime saw an empty directory. Pipelines that ran inside the API found the model and those routed to the runtime did not, so PharmaVigil triage was intermittently answered without its model.
fix: The local values mount the model volume on the API too, so both see the same files, and the runtime fetches a model it cannot see from the API with a token scoped to that model and caches it, so a volume mismatch can no longer silently disable a model.

title: Uploaded code and models depended on one pod's disk
problem: Code assets and ML models lived only on the data volume of the API pod that received them, so with several API replicas, a rescheduled pod or a volume that was not shared, a file could be missing on the pod asked to serve it and runs failed.
fix: Uploads, new versions and seeded files are mirrored to the configured object storage and restored by any pod that lacks them before serving, runtimes pull missing files with scoped tokens, seeds heal missing files, and both deploy scripts verify the runtime can read what the API stored.

title: Pipeline steps did not hold agents to their output schema
problem: An agent's output_schema was only checked on single-agent runs, the docs said pipelines checked it too, and a required field that was present but empty passed. PharmaVigil's coder could list a reaction as coded with no preferred term and the case carried it forward.
fix: A required field that is empty counts as a violation, an agent run as a pipeline step is checked against its schema and asked once to correct it, remaining violations are recorded on the step, and the MedDRA coder declares the schema a coded term must meet.

title: On multi-node AKS the API and worker ignored the shared data volume
problem: With sharedData.usePVC on, only the agent runtime pools mounted the shared Azure Files claim. The API, the worker and the cognify worker kept a per-node host path, so code assets and knowledge base uploads were only visible on the node that received them and were lost if the API moved node, and the runtime pools named the claim after the release while the claim itself was fixed.
fix: The API, worker and cognify worker mount the shared claim when it is enabled, the Azure values turn it on for all of them, the API's init container copies anything the older host path held without overwriting, and every pod uses the one claim name.

title: Code asset routes created their storage directory at import
problem: Importing the code asset router created /data/code-assets, so anything that loaded the module where /data is not writable failed before running, which broke the unit tests in CI.
fix: The directory is created on the first write instead of at import.

title: API requirements for CI had drifted from the image's dependencies
problem: The API image installs from pyproject.toml while CI installs apps/api/requirements.txt, which lacked stripe, celery, structlog, prometheus-client, python-dotenv, boto3 and nats-py, so tests touching those modules passed locally and failed in CI.
fix: requirements.txt lists every pyproject dependency and a CI check fails the build if they drift apart again.

title: GDPR erasure fails for any user with audit history
problem: gdpr_purge sets activity_logs.user_id to NULL but the column is NOT NULL, so the purge transaction aborts and nothing about the user is erased.
fix: Erasure replaces the actor with the nil id and clears ip and user agent under the audit maintenance flag. The audit chain commits to a salted digest of those fields so erasure keeps the chain verifiable.

title: Twelve agent-runtime tests fail and CI never runs them
problem: CI runs tests/unit only. apps/agent-runtime/tests has 12 failing tests across email sender SMTP, llm router default, MCP token encryption, sandboxed job gating, the token counter and pipeline node-complete callbacks, plus a stale cache key assertion.
fix: Triage each failure as a product bug or a stale test, fix it, and add the runtime suite to CI.

title: Live DAG watch stream holds a database transaction open for its whole life
problem: GET /api/executions/{id}/watch reads through the request session and then streams for as long as the tab is open. Each viewer pins a pooled connection idle in transaction. Two such sessions sat open for three hours and blocked a schema migration, which then deadlocked the rollout because the old pod stays until the new one is ready.
fix: Snapshots use a short session each and the request session is released before streaming. API and runtime connections set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout so a leak clears itself. The migrate step ends transactions idle for over five minutes and migrations run with a lock timeout so a blocked upgrade fails and retries instead of hanging.

title: Nothing stops two migrations from sharing a revision id
problem: A new migration reused an existing revision id. Alembic reported a cycle and the migrate init container failed on every restart. Only the rollout timeout showed it, and CI had no check.
fix: A unit test parses every migration, fails on a duplicate revision id, a missing parent or a cycle, and runs in CI.

title: Decision drafts never save from the browser
problem: The API's CORS preflight did not allow If-Match, so every draft save from the rule builder was blocked by the browser and the page showed Not saved.
fix: If-Match and If-None-Match added to allow_headers, ETag exposed, and a unit test checks that every header the web app sends is allowed.

title: Platform events never reached the NATS bus
problem: The event dispatcher connected to NATS without credentials, so every publish failed with Authorization Violation and opened a new connection per batch.
fix: It now connects with NATS_USER and NATS_PASSWORD, keeps one connection per event loop and logs a failed publish as a warning.

title: Code runner reaper crashed on a lower case LOG_LEVEL
problem: With LOG_LEVEL=debug the reaper CronJob and the runner exited at start with Unknown level, so idle runners were never scaled down.
fix: Both upper-case the level before handing it to logging.

title: deploy.sh called its own Grafana forward an unknown process
problem: The observability step asked for the Grafana forward again after setup_port_forwards had started it, found the port busy and printed an error.
fix: start_persistent_forward remembers what it started in the run and skips a repeat.

title: Eval cases saved from a run failed on the next run
problem: Save as eval case suggested max duration and cost at twice the captured run, with a 1 second floor. A 948 ms run gave a 1.9 s limit and reruns at 1.9 to 2 s failed with the right answer.
fix: Duration is now the largest of three times the run, the run plus 10 s, or 5 s. Cost is three times the run with a 0.01 floor. A unit test replays the case.

title: Every code asset, ML model and KB call opened a new database login
problem: invocation_log built a new engine for each logged call and disposed it, so every call paid a TCP connect plus a SCRAM login and a new Redis client. Under a 200 call burst the agent runtime spent most of its CPU on HMAC.
fix: One pooled engine and one Redis client per event loop. Warm code asset overhead fell from 27 ms to 3 ms p50.

title: Knowledge search and memory tools built an engine per call
problem: knowledge_search, hybrid_search, connector_call, meeting_speak and the memory tools created and disposed an engine on each call, three logins per KB search, and the memory tools leaked the pool on errors.
fix: They share engine.db_pool.shared_engine, and a runtime test fails if per-call engines come back.

title: Warm code calls queued on the database under load
problem: Each warm call read the asset row, its secrets and the sandbox settings, opened Redis, and updated the asset's last test row inline, so concurrent calls serialised on a six connection pool and one row lock.
fix: Asset, secrets and gate results are cached for 2 s with single flight (CODE_ASSET_CACHE_SECONDS), and the last test write runs in the background at most every 5 s. Burst throughput went from 22 to 57 calls a second on one runner.

title: The cluster API image still closed idle connections after 5 seconds
problem: The keep-alive fix went into apps/api/Dockerfile, but deploy.sh and deploy-azure.sh build docker/Dockerfile.api, which ran uvicorn with its 5 second default. Clients that reuse sockets saw resets, which showed up as socket hang up in specs and ReadError under load.
fix: docker/Dockerfile.api now runs with --timeout-keep-alive 75 and takes API_WORKERS. The code runner images upgrade OS packages and pip so the hardening check passes, and decision_load.py spreads connections over enough processes to measure the server rather than the client.

title: Under heavy load valid callers got 401 and 500
problem: At 2000 concurrent callers the capability and principal caches expired together, every request queried the db at once, the pool ran dry, and pool timeouts surfaced as 401 from the auth dependency and 500 elsewhere. The HTTP error handler also dropped Retry-After.
fix: Principal and capability loads are single flight per user, infrastructure errors in auth return 503 with Retry-After, a pool timeout anywhere returns 503 BUSY, and exception headers are kept.

title: NATS passwords were fixed strings in every cluster
problem: The chart shipped abenix-dev, coderun-dev and sys as NATS passwords, the application password sat in a ConfigMap, and queue_backend fell back to abenix-dev when NATS_PASSWORD was unset, so every Azure install had the same known credentials.
fix: NATS_PASSWORD, NATS_SYS_PASSWORD and the code runner password are generated on install into Secrets and kept across upgrades, nats.conf reads them from the environment, and the runtime no longer has a default password.

title: Expired approvals never emitted approval.resolved
problem: The expiry sweep updated rows in bulk without emitting the event, and an expired decision publish approval left its version in proposed.
fix: The sweep returns the rows it expired, emits approval.resolved with status expired in the same transaction, and runs the decision hook for decision_publish approvals.

title: Redelivering a dead webhook allowed one try
problem: Redeliver reset the status but not the attempt counter, so a replayed dead delivery failed straight back to dead after one attempt.
fix: Redeliver resets attempts so a replay gets the full retry budget.

title: Switching a subscription to webhook hid its signing secret
problem: Changing the target to webhook through PUT minted a signing secret that was never returned, so the receiver could not verify signatures.
fix: PUT returns the new secret once, the same as create.

title: Reference sets could not be deleted
problem: There was no way to remove a reference set from the UI or API, so old sets piled up.
fix: DELETE refuses with 409 naming the decisions while an active version uses the set, and the Reference sets page has Delete set with an inline confirm.

title: Pipelines could not declare input parameters
problem: Pipeline mode had no input editor, yet chat and the SDK playground read declared inputs, so typed pipeline inputs were impossible to set up in the UI.
fix: A shared input variables editor appears on the pipeline overview and the agent config panel, and removing every parameter now clears them on save.

title: Pipeline step JSON fields dropped keystrokes
problem: Any keystroke that left a step's JSON field invalid was thrown away, so facts and arguments could not be typed.
fix: The field keeps the typed text and shows an inline error until it parses.

title: Decision keys in pipeline steps were free text
problem: A decision step needed the key typed by hand with no hint of what exists, whether it is published, or which facts it needs.
fix: The step offers a dropdown of the tenant's decisions, warns when one is not published and lists its required facts, which the decision list now returns.

title: SDK playground missed agents and mishandled inputs
problem: It loaded only the first 100 agents, sent the first declared input as the message and left it out of the context, and generated code always used a placeholder message.
fix: It loads every page of agents, sends all inputs as context with a separate message box, and the Python, TypeScript and Java snippets carry exactly what was run.

title: Decision risk tier could not be changed
problem: The create dialog said the tier could be changed later but no control existed.
fix: The tier badge on a decision is a picker for users who can publish.

title: web reloads after the first deployed stale code
problem: minikube image load keeps a tag it already has, so rebuilding at the same commit never reached the pod.
fix: deploy.sh streams the image with docker save and docker load.

title: approval_gate failed with 401 inside agent runs
problem: The tool said the runtime filled in the execution, agent and auth token, but it did not. Without an explicit auth_token it fell back to INTERNAL_API_TOKEN, which the API does not accept, so creating the approval failed and nothing linked it to the run.
fix: approval_gate is built per run with its execution, agent, tenant and user, links the approval to the execution, and calls the API with a short-lived token for the run's user. Explicit arguments still win.

title: Named in-cluster webhook receivers could not be saved
problem: Delivery honoured EVENTS_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS but saving a subscription still refused every .cluster.local, .internal and .local name, so only bare service names worked.
fix: Saving a subscription honours the same exact-name allowlist.

title: until_gate never saw human_approval gates
problem: execute with wait_mode until_gate only watched the approvals table, so a run paused on a human_approval gate, which lives in Redis, looked like it was still running until the wait timed out.
fix: The watcher also checks the run's Redis gates and returns paused_at with the hitl id that approvals.signoff accepts.

title: GDPR purge soft-deleted every agent memory on the platform
problem: The Postgres step ran UPDATE agent_memories with no filter, so purging one person soft-deleted every tenant's agent memories.
fix: Agent memories are purged only for agents the person created in that tenant.

title: GDPR purge could target a user in another tenant
problem: Both purge endpoints accepted any user id without checking the subject belonged to the caller's tenant.
fix: Both endpoints check the subject is in the caller's tenant.

title: GDPR Neo4j and Pinecone steps never purged anything
problem: The Neo4j step imported a missing atlas neo4j_client and the Pinecone step a missing pinecone_client, so both recorded 0 and left the person's data in place, and purge_log had no count column.
fix: The Neo4j step deletes Cognify entities naming the person and the matching Postgres graph rows, Pinecone deletes the person's persona vectors, and every step records a true affected_count shown on /settings/gdpr.

title: atlas_cypher and atlas_as_of always failed
problem: Both imported a module that does not exist, and Atlas lives in Postgres so Cypher never applied.
fix: atlas_as_of answers from atlas snapshots and live tables, atlas_cypher is removed because free Cypher on the shared graph cannot be scoped to a tenant safely.

title: Extractors, reranker, document ACL and Cognify settings were never used
problem: The extractors, reranker, document_access pre-filter and cognify_config values existed but nothing called them, and the old ACL rule would have hidden every document from users without a full grant.
fix: Ingest uses the extractors, search reranks and cites, documents with grants are filtered before ranking with a corrected rule, and Cognify honours confidence threshold, conflict action, parallelism and daily budget.

title: KB re-embed was a stub and Pinecone vacuum never ran
problem: kb_reembed returned queued without doing anything, the vacuum body was pass, and neither task was included or routed to a queue the worker consumes.
fix: Re-embed re-reads and re-chunks every document and switches the collection in one step with progress in the UI, and the vacuum runs daily at 02:30 UTC from the API scheduler.

title: Pinecone search returned no matches
problem: An operator precedence bug read SDK response objects as empty, so Pinecone-backed collections returned nothing.
fix: Matches are read correctly from SDK and dict responses.

title: Celery queue backend could never run agents
problem: CeleryBackend imported a task that does not exist and no worker consumed its queues, so a celery install sat idle.
fix: Agent execution runs on NATS only, celery fails fast with a clear message, and helm refuses remote execution without NATS.

title: Queued runs were lost when a runtime pod crashed
problem: Messages were acked when a run started, so a crash lost the run until the sweeper failed it.
fix: Messages are acked after the run with heartbeats and a lease on the execution row, so another pod takes over a dead pod's run.

title: Trace context stopped at the queue
problem: inject_carrier and extract_carrier were never called, so a trace ended at the API.
fix: traceparent rides the NATS envelope and child agent calls, so one trace spans API, queue, runtime and child runs.

title: Backups could not run
problem: The backup CronJobs mounted a PVC nothing created, and the Neo4j dump ran in a pod without the data volume on an edition that cannot dump online.
fix: The chart creates the backup PVC and Neo4j is exported over Bolt with APOC.

title: decisions.review gated nothing
problem: The capability was in the catalog but no endpoint checked it.
fix: Signing a decision publish approval needs decisions.review plus the tier's signing capability.

title: Admin tool runtime and scaling pipelines were open to any user
problem: C:/Program Files/Git/api/admin/tool-runtime and /api/admin/scaling/pipelines only checked sign-in.
fix: They require admin, and a test asserts every admin route returns 403 to a non-admin.

title: Toasts never showed and session expiry went to a missing page
problem: ToastProvider was never mounted and a failed refresh redirected to /login, which does not exist.
fix: One toast stack is mounted app-wide, and an expired session returns to the sign-in form with a notice and back to the page afterwards.

title: Settings showed Events to users who cannot use it
problem: The settings sub-nav listed Webhooks to everyone while the sidebar gated it on events.manage.
fix: The entry is renamed Events and gated, and the page explains how to get access.

title: API metrics saw one worker and two alerts could never fire
problem: The cluster API image set no PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR, and PostgresDown and RedisDown used a metric nothing exported.
fix: The image runs multi-process metrics, and a dependency probe exports abenix_health_check for Postgres and Redis.

title: Network policies blocked the platform's own traffic
problem: With policies on, runtime and worker pods matched no rule, nothing allowed NATS, Prometheus scrapes were blocked, and names collided with the bitnami policies.
fix: The policies are rewritten with shared egress, a NATS policy, renamed data store policies and a rendering test of required and blocked flows.

title: Web build settings never reached the bundle
problem: docker/Dockerfile.web took no build args, so NEXT_PUBLIC values did nothing.
fix: The image takes the five NEXT_PUBLIC values as build args and the deploy scripts pass them.

title: Agent budget limits were never enforced
problem: daily_cost_limit, daily_budget_usd and per_execution_cost_limit were stored but never checked.
fix: Daily caps are enforced at every run entry point with BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the per-run cap stops pipelines.

title: Pipeline runs skipped the moderation gate
problem: The tenant moderation policy was applied inside the agent executor only, so a pipeline run took its message and inputs to every step unchecked, PII included.
fix: Pipeline runs pass the gate before they start. A block refuses the run with 422 MODERATION_BLOCKED, a redact masks the message and every text input, and the events are recorded.

title: The UX walkthrough left a redact policy active for the whole tenant
problem: Its cleanup deleted the policy, but a policy with recorded events cannot be deleted, so every run left its policy active and the tenant default switched off, changing the outcome of later specs.
fix: The walkthrough remembers the active policies, switches its own off and the old ones back on in afterAll, even when a test fails.
